claims.claim: The application runs its agent harness locally and can use user-selected model providers.
Commander, Manager, Specialist, and Worker organization roles can govern typed delegation without granting tool permissions.
Consequential delegated tasks can use task contracts, deterministic acceptance checks, bounded revisions, and optional independent audit.
Control Mode exposes evidence-backed read-only agent, memory-provenance, approval, action, cost, and provider-signal surfaces without inventing unavailable runtime state.
Derivative orchestration does not bypass the inherited capability, consent, permission, or E-STOP boundaries.

Private Moe AI Station development prefers reusing compatible StarNet runtime, tools, providers, permissions, workflows, memory, channels, MCP, UI and other proven subsystems instead of replacing them without functional need.
The private fork does not automatically consume StarNet upstream release artifacts through the detached updater path.
A separately signed Moe AI Station public update channel is not required for the private-use target.
Full independent branding is not required for the private-use target; redistribution remains outside scope.
A forced application-identifier/data-path migration is not required for the private-use target and should not risk existing compatible state without a functional reason.

distributionNote: Public redistribution is not a project goal. If that goal changes, branding, licensing, signing/update provenance and app-identity migration must be reassessed before distribution.
